title: [23/10/2024] UK birth rate of women in 6 different age groups
prompt: The graph below shows the changes in the birth rates for women in 6 different age groups in the UK from 1973 to 2008.
Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the birth rates per 1000 people for six different age groups of women in the United Kingdom over a 35-year period, from 1973 to 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while birth rates among women aged 30-35 and 35-39 increased steadily, those for younger women under 25 declined significantly. Additionally, women aged 25-29 consistently maintained the highest birth rates.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the groups with higher birth rates, women aged 25-29 recorded approximately 140 births per 1,000 people in 1973, followed by the 20-25 age group at about 130 births, while the 30-35 group started at around 70 births. The 25-29 age group, despite maintaining the highest figures, showed a generally downward trend with some fluctuations, ending at about 120 births in 2008. The 20-25 age group saw a consistent decline to approximately 92 births, while in contrast, the 30-35 group demonstrated a steady increase, reaching roughly 88 births by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining age groups, both women under 20 and those aged 35-39 began with similar birth rates of about 60 and 40 births per 1,000 people respectively in 1973. The youngest group experienced a significant decline, falling to approximately 35 births by 2008, while the 35-39 age group showed an upward trend, rising to about 65 births. The birth rate for women aged 40 and over remained consistently the lowest throughout the period, staying below 20 births per 1,000 people and declining from about 20 to 5 births over the period.
